Joint random-effects covariance with ordinal biomarkers (Gaussian copula)

Source: R/copulaLongitudinal.R
longitudinalSubVarCopula.Rd

Re-estimates the shared random-effects covariance D across all biomarkers by maximum likelihood, holding each biomarker's fixed effects, residual variance and (for an ordinal biomarker) thresholds at their separate-fit values, as longitudinalSubVar() does for continuous ones. An ordinal observation is the category of a latent score \(Z = \eta + \epsilon\), \(\epsilon \sim N(0, 1)\) (probit link, Albert & Chib), observed only through the thresholds that bracket it, so the posterior of the random effects given the data is not Gaussian and the EM's \(E[b b^T \mid y]\) has no closed form. It is computed by

  • copula_D_aghq(), an EM with adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature over the ordinal biomarkers' random effects (the continuous biomarkers' random effects are integrated out exactly), when those number at most max_quadrature_dim; deterministic, with the usual convergence check;

  • otherwise copula_D_saem(), a stochastic-approximation EM (SAEM) that draws the latent scores, whose cost does not grow with that dimension.

Both target the same maximum-likelihood estimate, but with the default number of iterations SAEM stopped short of it: for two ordinal biomarkers with a random intercept and slope each (four ordinal random effects), the random-effects variances were off by about 5\ quadrature (\(5^4 = 625\) nodes per subject) removes; hence the default max_quadrature_dim = 4. The earlier version plugged in the mean of each latent score given its category, which ignored the score's own variance and underestimated the ordinal biomarkers' random-effects variances (by about 40\ for a random slope in simulations).

Usage

longitudinalSubVarCopula(
  thetaLong,
  l,
  biomarker_type,
  thresholds,
  tol.em = 1e-04,
  max.iter = 500,
  max_quadrature_dim = 4,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

thetaLong

List with the stacked fixed effects beta, the starting D and the residual variances sigma2 (1 for an ordinal biomarker).

l

Per-subject design bookkeeping built by longitudinalSubCopula(); l$yik[[m]] holds an ordinal biomarker's category codes.

biomarker_type, thresholds

As stored in the fit.

tol.em, max.iter

Convergence tolerance on D and iteration cap of the quadrature EM.

max_quadrature_dim

Largest number of ordinal random effects handled by quadrature.

verbose

Print the change in D at every iteration.

Value

A list with the estimate D.
